seo_description: ClipMergeEditor is a free, open-source Mac clipboard tool. Select several clips, merge them with a separator, clean up the text, and paste it as one.
hero_sub: Select several items from your clipboard history, merge them with the separator you choose, tidy the result in the built-in editor, and paste it as one clip. Press ⌘⇧M to open it.
features_sub: Everything is built around one workflow: combine copied text, clean it up, and put it back on the clipboard.

features.title: Multi-select and merge
features.desc: Hold ⌘ or ⇧ to pick several clips, then join them in the order copied or the order selected. Choose New Line, Blank Line, Comma and Space, Tab, or your own separator.

features.title: Built-in text editor
features.desc: The merged result opens in a monospaced editor with standard undo and a live line and character count. You can also open any single clip in it.

features.title: One-click cleanup tools
features.desc: Trim whitespace, remove duplicate lines (keeping the first), sort lines, or number them. Then Copy the result or Save as Clip to add it to your history.

features.title: Global hotkey and menu bar
features.desc: Open the window from anywhere with ⌘⇧M, or change the shortcut in Settings. The menu bar item lists your last five clips for quick copy and lets you pause recording.

features.title: Privacy-minded recording
features.desc: Concealed and transient pasteboard types, such as those from password managers, are skipped. You can also ignore specific apps by name or bundle identifier.

features.title: Searchable clipboard history
features.desc: Keeps up to 200 text clips (10 to 200, configurable), with search, optional duplicate skipping, and launch at login. Only plain text is recorded.

permissions_step: No special permissions are required; the app reads the clipboard but never asks for Accessibility, Screen Recording, or Microphone access.

faq.q: Is ClipMergeEditor really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no account, subscription, or paid tier. If you find it useful, there is an optional Support / Donate button in the menu bar and in Settings.

None beyond normal clipboard access. It does not use Accessibility, Screen Recording, or Microphone, and its global hotkey works without Accessibility permission. It never pastes automatically; it only writes to the clipboard when you press Copy or pick a menu bar clip.
Your history is a JSON file at ~/Library/Application Support/ClipMergeEditor/history.json on your Mac. The app makes no network connections, so nothing leaves your machine.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it from source with Xcode.
